This replaces that method.\n\nA static audit read the whole harness across ten dimensions with no GPU and no\nmodel calls: govern's control flow, its budgets and exit codes, every gate for\nvacuous passes and for false alarms, the SPECs, the launchers, the tests,\nobservability, resource safety, and the gap against ordinary orchestrator\npractice. 171 findings, each handed to an independent skeptic whose brief was to\nREFUTE it. 74 were refuted. 97 survived and merged into 52 defects.\n\nThe tier-1 defects are the ones that explain the day:\n\n- The model gate FAILED OPEN on any non-zero exit, so a crashed audit could\n  promote un-audited work.\n- The \"a model cannot audit its own work\" guard compared engine-qualified\n  strings, so in the default configuration gemma4-26b gated its own work and the\n  guard stayed silent.\n- Checker.report() returned 0 when zero checks ran — a gate that verified\n  nothing reported success.\n- harness-canary, the tool that checks the harness, failed OPEN when dcode was\n  absent, and printed \"every gate fired\" from a partial run.\n- Three defects fixed earlier today were still live in the paths nobody looked\n  at: exit 124 misread as a clock in the gate phase and in brief/survey, bin/eval\n  telling a model to run code in a session with no execute tool, and four of five\n  launchers still hanging on an inherited stdin.\n\nWork and evidence stopped being destroyed: failed-tier*/ and stopped-tier*/ are\narchived rather than overwritten, the model gate takes a pre-gate copy, telemetry\nis atomic and fail-closed, and an interrupted run now records that it was\ninterrupted instead of vanishing.\n\nRuns stopped being wasted: validate.sh was the only unbounded budget in the\nscript; budget.env silently overrode explicit env; --start-tier and\n--max-escalations were unvalidated so the escalation-budget test failed OPEN.\n\nGuards that did not exist: a per-slice lock and a box-level GPU lock (two runs on\ndifferent slices could still stack, which is how the box overheated), a thermal\npreflight, and signal traps — killing govern used to orphan dcode holding the GPU.\n\nItem 50 mattered more than its rank: slices resolved lib as installed-first, so\nevery gate ran the stale ~/.local copy and repo changes to invariants.py were\ninert. installed and repo now agree on every slice.\n\nThree adversarial rounds, each re-verifying the last rather than trusting it:\n97 -> 11 -> 9 -> 0 open. Each round caught fixes that reintroduced the defect they\nremoved — a fixed-name pre-gate tree, a vacuous cap check whose docstring claimed\notherwise, a lock that named the wrong process. It also caught the verification\nidiom I had been using all day: `echo \"$(basename $d) exit=$?\"` expands basename\nfirst, so $? is always 0 and every slice reports green.\n\nVerified CPU-only: 175 tests pass (was 145), zero syntax failures, 7 of 10 slice\ngates green with installed==repo everywhere, harness-canary --fast honest about\nwhat it skipped, staleness-check clean. The three red gates are unimplemented\nwork/ trees, proven pre-existing by running each slice's HEAD gate against them.\n\nNOT verified, and not claimed: everything downstream of a real dcode call — the\nexit-code taxonomy branches, classify_124's transcript read, kill_child against a\nlive process tree, the thermal preflight's cooldown loop, the GPU lock under real\ncontention, and readiness's \"governed runs\" criterion, which cannot go green\nwithout a run.",

      "message": "Keep each run's evidence, spend the cheap checks first, add the mix slice\n\nFive governed runs today produced four failures and none of them was the model:\na gate that cried wolf, a spec with two readings, a misdiagnosed turn cap, and a\nsession teardown. Three were diagnosable from one run's artifacts without\nspending another — except the artifacts did not survive to be diagnosed.\n\ngovern wrote transcripts, validate output and tool counts to FIXED names, so\nevery run destroyed its predecessor. Run 4's 36-tool-call transcript, the only\nfull record of ornith attempting run_eval, was overwritten by run 5 before it\ncould be read. Only telemetry was ever timestamped. Each run now archives the\nprevious set to .artifacts/prev-<RUN_ID>/ first.\n\ngovern also runs `harness-canary --fast` as a preflight. It costs about a second\nand proves the session gates still fire; a governed run costs 10-45 minutes of\nsustained GPU load, and the box reaches 80C doing it. Advisory, not fatal, but\nnever silent — if a gate is not firing, findings from the run that follows\ndescribe the harness rather than the model.\n\nslices/polars-mix: data/mix.py, chosen because it is stdlib-only with no\nsandbox, no venv and no PATH gymnastics, so a failure is about the model rather\nthan about plumbing. 32 checks, 31 fail against the stub.\n\nIts first run scored 21/32 with 212 lines written unassisted before the clock\ncut it off at 1802s, and the 11 failures reduce to ONE real defect\n(_assert_provenance_complete takes a single record where the contract says a\ncollection) plus one check for a rule added afterwards. The other three failures\nthe gate first reported were mine:\n\n- a rec() helper whose positional `source` collided with over={\"source\": None},\n  reported as an implementation TypeError;\n- `raises()` accepting ANY exception, so ten R4 checks passed because the\n  implementation choked on the argument shape rather than because it refused.\n  Only ValueError counts as a refusal now; TypeError and AttributeError mean the\n  call was malformed;\n- a SPEC whose per-builder cap was UNSATISFIABLE with one domain builder —\n  builder == domain_total, so `builder <= 0.5 * domain` holds only at zero. The\n  implementation correctly zeroed the domain portion and the gate called it a\n  bug. The rule now says the cap applies only with two or more builders.\n\nAlso stops tests/test_govern_turn_cap.py littering: its shim wrote run_eval.py\nthrough a relative path and leaked one into the repo root.",

      "message": "Stop reading every exit 124 as a clock, and stop discarding the work\n\nThird govern run, ornith, zero swaps. The gate-failure path has always kept its evidence; the 124 path threw\n517 seconds of working implementation away without a trace.\n\ntests/test_govern_turn_cap.py drives the real work block through PATH shims and\ncovers both directions — a turn cap must not read as a breach, and a genuine\nbreach must not be relabelled a turn cap.",

      "message": "Schedule the spread tests for Fri 2026-08-14 10:00 ET, with an unattended-safe wrapper\n\nRunning these unattended has one real hazard: both scripts open live positions,\nand if a close does not fill, the leftover sits with the daemon stopped and\nnobody watching. If the leftover is the SHORT leg of a vertical whose long leg\ndid close, that is a naked short. Two things therefore have to hold no matter\nhow the run ends:\n\n  1. The daemon comes back. `trap restore EXIT INT TERM` fires on success,\n     failure, timeout and kill, and systemd's TimeoutStartSec=3000 is the\n     backstop above the scripts' own 1500s/900s timeouts.\n  2. Nothing new is left open. spread_cleanup snapshots Account B's option\n     positions BEFORE the daemon is stopped, and afterwards flattens anything\n     that appeared since — shorts first, market orders, because a naked short\n     is unbounded risk while a stranded long is only the premium. Positions the\n     account already held are never touched. A missing or unreadable snapshot\n     REFUSES to flatten rather than treating all three existing positions as\n     new, which is the failure that would turn a safety net into a liquidation.\n\nA leftover also writes logs/SPREAD_TESTS_NEEDS_ATTENTION and fires notify-send,\nbecause \"it is in the log\" is not good enough for a naked short nobody is\nlooking for.\n\nScheduled at 10:00 ET, not 09:30. Opening-auction spreads are unrepresentatively\nwide and the probe measures fills against the quoted mid, so running into the\nopen would bias the result toward FAIL and teach us nothing about normal-session\nexecution. Delivered as a systemd user timer with a fixed OnCalendar date, so it\nis genuinely one-shot — a recurring cron entry would stop the daemon and submit\norders every weekday. Persistent=false, so a machine asleep at 10:00 does not\nwake up and trade at an unknown hour.\n\nRehearsed end to end twice, once through bash and once through systemd (whose\nenvironment differs and is where this breaks): snapshot → daemon stop → probe →\nverify → cleanup → daemon restored. Both scripts correctly refused on the\nclosed market, the trap ran, and the daemon came back active. Also verified the\nmissing-snapshot guard refuses instead of flattening the account.\n\n134 passed.",

      "message": "Rebuild the Phase 0 probe (ladder, round trip, min-fills); add live Phase 2/3 verification\n\nPhase 0 probe. The first run produced a verdict from ONE fill out of four, and\nthe name that filled — INTC — is the one that does not need a spread. It also\nmeasured entry cost only: it reported -2.30% where the actual round trip was\n-5.9%. Three fixes:\n\n  * MIN_FILLS = 3. Below that the result is INCONCLUSIVE, which is reported as\n    a distinct outcome from FAIL. \"Not measured\" and \"measured and rejected\"\n    are different facts and the first run conflated them.\n  * The gate is on the ROUND TRIP, mid-referenced so a move during the ~1\n    minute hold does not contaminate it. GATE_ROUND_TRIP 6% = the original 3%\n    per side, paid once in and once out. Entry-only cost and raw realized P&L\n    are both still reported so the two runs stay comparable.\n  * A real ladder. One limit held 45s cannot fill a wide package. The limit now\n    escalates from the net mid toward the legging-in worst case, and holds\n    longer per rung the wider the package is (25s / 50s / 100s). The ladder\n    runs all the way TO the worst case rather than stopping at the gate —\n    capping it at the threshold would only ever let us observe fills that pass,\n    which measures our own assumption instead of the market.\n\nAlso: names holding an open position are skipped (NVDA and TSM both have one in\nB, and probing them would collide with position tracking), and the default list\nnow leads with names that actually need a spread instead of cheap controls.\n\nPhase 2/3 verification is new — sigma/ops/spread_verify.py. The probe asks\nwhether the BROKER fills a vertical sanely; this asks whether OUR code can live\nwith the resulting position, which is the dangerous half: a spread the system\ncannot close is what stranded old Account C, and one it half-closes leaves a\nnaked short. It drives the production path deliberately —\n_build_spread_from_candidate, _execute_spread_order, load_positions,\ncheck_ticker_exposure, close_position — because a hand-rolled order would prove\nthe broker works and prove nothing about us. Seven checks: ENTRY, GROUPING,\nLEGS, RISK (max_risk is the net debit, not the long premium and not the sum of\nboth legs), EXPOSURE (counted once), EXIT, ATOMIC, NO SHORT.\n\nBoth scripts now refuse to run when the daemon is up or the market is shut,\nrather than trusting the operator to remember. Verified in both directions.\n--dry-run on spread_verify exercises the pairing and the cap check without\nsubmitting anything, so the riskiest logic can be proven while the market is\nclosed.\n\nDry runs tonight, all pairing cleanly and all inside the $1,292 cap:\n  AMD  $490/$500 net $423   (outright would be $3,161)\n  AMAT $520/$530 net $599   (outright $5,307)\n  LRCX $340/$350 net $440   (outright $2,712)\n  PANW $400/$410 net $457   (outright $2,834)\n  INTC $105/$110 net $219\n\nBUG FOUND BY THE SWALLOWED-EXCEPTION LOGGING, fixed here: get_stock_price\ncalled StockLatestRequest / get_stock_latest, neither of which exists in\nalpaca-py. The ImportError went into a silent handler, so EVERY spot price in\nthe system fell through to the bars path and returned the last DAILY CLOSE\ninstead of the live price — feeding strike selection, moneyness and the\naffordability caps. Now uses StockLatestTradeRequest with a quote-midpoint\nfallback before bars. Measured after the fix: NVDA $225.36 live vs $224.09\nprior close, MSFT $496.81 vs $492.43 — a 0.9% error on a quiet day.\n\n134 passed.",

      "message": "Fix two stale inputs that inverted R-ALLOC-1's conclusion\n\nR-ALLOC-1 has been quoted for weeks as the largest measured improvement in the\nproject — fleet Sharpe 0.77 -> 1.25, \"capital allocated inversely to quality\".\nBoth halves of that rested on inputs that had gone stale.\n\n1. LIVE_EQUITY was a hardcoded ledger last checked 2026-07-18. The \"current\"\n   candidate IS that split, so the constant does not merely mislabel a baseline —\n   it fabricates the finding. By 2026-07-25 it described a fleet that no longer\n   existed: core_allocation $1,500 -> $15,000 and options_income $16,000 ->\n   $148,000, moving options from 30.5% to 56.3% of the fleet. Now fetched from\n   the brokers per book, with the constants demoted to a per-book fallback so one\n   unreachable venue degrades that book rather than failing the study.\n   (--stale-equity reproduces the old behaviour.)\n\n2. _options_income_series() modelled {\"exit_mode\": \"expiry\"} — the MONTHLY\n   baseline — while the live book now runs R-OPT-2's weekly ladder. Weighting a\n   strategy that is not deployed understated that book badly: standalone Sharpe\n   0.25 -> 0.73 once the series matches reality, because the ladder halves dollar\n   drawdown at ~2x total P&L. The series now follows options_income_entry_freq,\n   so it tracks the deployed config instead of drifting from it.\n\nCorrected result, both fixes applied:\n    current       Sharpe 1.20  CAGR 3.48%  maxDD -4.8%\n    equal_weight  Sharpe 1.49  CAGR 4.73%  maxDD -4.6%\n    risk_parity   Sharpe 1.42  CAGR 4.39%  maxDD -5.1%\n    max_sharpe    Sharpe 1.45  CAGR 6.61%  maxDD -7.3%  (core pinned near cap)\n\nversus the previously reported current 0.77 / risk_parity 1.26. The remaining\nallocation gap is +0.29 Sharpe (current -> equal_weight), not +0.48, and the\nrecommended rule flips from risk_parity to equal_weight. Deploying the ladder had\nalready captured much of what the reallocation was being credited for.\n\nNo capital moved — still an operator decision, now on numbers that describe the\nactual fleet.\n\nSuite: 1119 passed (4 pre-existing test_r_opt_2 failures unchanged).",

      "message": "Add Sentry absence detection; error capture alone could not catch the outage\n\nSentry was already wired — SDK installed, _init_sentry() in the worker, FastAPI\nintegrations in the API, divergence capture in book_reconcile. Only the DSN was\nmissing. But reviewing it surfaced that the existing setup could not have caught\nthe failure it most needed to.\n\nOn 2026-06-04 the worker stopped. Nothing noticed for seven weeks. It logged ZERO\nerrors, because it did not fail — it simply ceased. Exception capture structurally\ncannot detect that: it fires when something runs and breaks, never when something\nis absent. Redis heartbeats exist but only help someone who thinks to look.\n\nSo the tick loop now emits a Sentry cron check-in per unit alongside each\nheartbeat. Sentry raises an issue when an expected check-in does NOT arrive, which\ninverts the problem from \"detect a failure\" to \"detect silence\". One monitor per\nunit (per asset class / branch), so a single wedged book is distinguishable from a\nwhole dead worker. Best-effort and fully swallowed — monitoring must never break\nwhat it monitors, which is tested.\n\nAlso fixed in the existing init:\n  - AsyncioIntegration is NOT a sentry-sdk default (verified against\n    _DEFAULT_INTEGRATIONS); without it an unhandled exception inside a spawned\n    task reaches only asyncio's handler and never Sentry. Now requested\n    explicitly. LoggingIntegration IS default, so the logger.exception calls the\n    tick loop already emits were being captured.\n  - `release` is tagged from the booted git sha, so \"which commit started this\"\n    is answerable from the issue. This required reordering main(): _init_sentry()\n    ran BEFORE _ensure_git_sha(), so the release tag would have been empty on\n    every event. Pinned by a test.\n\ndoctor.py now validates the DSN is USABLE rather than merely non-empty — a\nmalformed or revoked DSN makes init() a silent no-op that looks identical to\nworking monitoring until the incident you needed it for. Verified both ways:\n\"not-a-dsn\" -> BadDsn, well-formed -> host/project/env reported. A second check\nasserts the check-in is actually wired into the loop, so the function cannot exist\nuncalled while looking instrumented.\n\nStill inert until SENTRY_DSN is set — that requires a Sentry project, which is\nthe operator's to create.\n\nSuite: 1119 passed, +12 new.
